Appendix A. Reproduction and migration notes

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-09-reproduce.Rmd
book-09-reproduce.Rmd

What you will learn

Rebuild the offline book and recognise the old recipe conventions.

This chapter uses the 24-person synthetic questionnaire test fixture described in Getting started. You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the book-work directory created in Getting started. Run this setup first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture()
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

The site connection is ready. This chapter creates its temporary questionnaire fixture locally.

Source and rendered lessons

The editable chapters are vignettes/book-*.Rmd.orig. The precompute script executes them against the synthetic fixture and writes .Rmd with the actual output embedded. The resulting files contain ordinary Markdown code fences, so the website does not connect to a database when it builds.

From the book client checkout, run tools/book/run-pod.sh in this workspace, or run Rscript tools/book/precompute.R in an R environment containing the matching packages and fixture dependencies. Then run Rscript tools/book/build-site.R to build the site and its helper downloads, followed by Rscript tools/book/verify-bundle.R to execute every chapter from the final ZIP. The pod driver is workspace-specific; the R scripts and fixture are portable.

Record the software versions 

vapply(c("dsOMOP", "dsOMOPClient", "DSI", "DSLite", "dsBase", "dsBaseClient"),
       function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)), character(1))
#>       dsOMOP dsOMOPClient          DSI       DSLite       dsBase dsBaseClient 
#>     "2.10.4"     "2.10.4"      "1.8.0"      "1.5.0"      "6.3.5"      "6.3.5"

These are the actual versions used for this rendering. Detailed assertions, source hashes and test logs are retained under tools/book/evidence.

Reproduce both practice resources

Run Rscript tools/book/load-practice.R ../practice-data. The loader pins the EunomiaDatasets source revision and verifies SHA-256 for both archives. It creates gibleed.sqlite, numeric.sqlite and manifest.json in ../practice-data. If you chose a different loader directory, set BOOK_PRACTICE_DIR to that directory before running the lessons. These are administrator-side operations on public synthetic data, separate from analyst DataSHIELD calls. The following table reads your loader’s manifest from that same directory. The checkout’s tools/book/evidence/book2/practice-manifest.json is historical build evidence; readers do not need it.

practice_dir <- Sys.getenv("BOOK_PRACTICE_DIR", file.path("..", "practice-data"))
manifest <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(practice_dir, "manifest.json"))
loaded <- do.call(rbind, lapply(manifest, function(x) data.frame(
  Dataset = x$dataset, Measurements = x$measurements$rows,
  Numeric = x$measurements$numeric_values,
  Numeric_with_unit = x$measurements$numeric_with_unit)))
knitr::kable(loaded, row.names = FALSE)
Dataset Measurements Numeric Numeric_with_unit
GiBleed 44053 0 0
Synthea27Nj 10040 9107 8403

GiBleed supplies the basics; Synthea27Nj supplies numeric labs. Its numeric values and mapped units come from the pinned source, without fabricated lab extensions. The questionnaire fixture remains separate and is explicitly named in its lessons.

The loader, two-resource DSLite helper and questionnaire fixture are downloadable from this site. The same SQLite files can be mounted into another Rock server; their resource registration is shown in chapter 0. Dependencies are listed in tools/book/README.md.

The local test driver

DSLite 1.5 rejects some quoted dsBase call strings containing commas. The practice helper applies the same scoped lexer repair used by the package’s release tests. It changes tokenisation only: ds.table, assignments and all disclosure checks still run for real. It does not apply to Opal. The two intentional refusal chunks in chapter 12 omit DSLite’s extra missing-symbol cleanup warnings; they display the actual policy error, and the verification checks that no refused output exists. The helper also injects a synthetic test pseudonym root; a deployed server manages its own private root automatically.

Migrating older recipes

The 2.10.2 colleague example selected a categorical observation with omop_variable(table = ..., concept_id = ..., format = "last_value", value_source = ...). Its translation path required an output name ending in _concept_id. The death feature needed value_source = "cause_concept_id"; column alone did not select the reduced value. Those are legacy conventions, not the API taught here.

In language 2, use event = omop_event(...) and reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"). Use format = "wide" and grain = "person" on the output. Concept typing now supplies labels regardless of the output name. Re-execute an old recipe to obtain new labelled assignments; renaming an existing symbol does not recompute it.

Calendar migration also matters. first_date and last_date remain day offsets. For calendar values use omop_date(), for calendar precision use omop_date_spec(), and for completed age at death use omop_age_at("death"). Do not relabel annual year subtraction as completed age.

Inspect the executed language 

check <- omop_recipe(variables = list(age = omop_age_at("death")),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
recipe_explain(check, conns = conns)$selected
#> [1] "v2"
stopifnot(recipe_explain(check, conns = conns)$selected == "v2")
print(recipe_execute(check, out = c(people = "D_migration"), conns = conns))
#>        people 
#> "D_migration"

If an explanation selects v1, it is explaining the legacy execution path. Merely printing a forced v2 conversion would not prove that the actual execution uses it.

Recap

The editable source executes once; the generated website is offline. Migration changes the recipe definitions, not just column names.

Try it

Check that the migration recipe is native before using it.

Solution

recipe_explain(check, conns = conns)$selected
#> [1] "v2"
